steps: The existence of an element in two or more forms having different physical properties but the same chemical composition is called allotropy.
Carbon exists in crystalline forms, such as diamond, graphite and fullerene, and in amorphous forms, such as coal.
In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four other carbon atoms in a three-dimensional structure. Diamond is very hard and does not conduct electricity.
In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms in layers. Graphite is soft and conducts electricity.
Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon in which carbon atoms form cage-like molecules, such as C₆₀.
Sulphur exists mainly in two allotropic forms: rhombic sulphur and monoclinic sulphur.
Rhombic sulphur consists of yellow crystals and is stable below 96°C.
Monoclinic sulphur consists of yellow, needle-shaped crystals and is stable from 96°C to about 119°C. On cooling below 96°C, it changes into rhombic sulphur.
Coal is an impure, amorphous form of carbon; it is black and comparatively soft.
Diamond is a pure, crystalline form of carbon; it is transparent and extremely hard.
items.finalAnswer: Carbon and sulphur each have different allotropic forms; coal is impure, amorphous and soft, whereas diamond is pure, crystalline and extremely hard.

steps: The solubility of a solute is the number of grams of that solute which dissolve in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a particular temperature.
As temperature increases, the solubility of most solid solutes in water increases.
The solubility of gases generally decreases as temperature increases.
items.finalAnswer: The solubility of most solids increases with temperature, while the solubility of gases generally decreases.
